lacuna.name: graph-node-concurrency
lacuna.repo_anchor: Constraint frame (the anchor, quoted): "vLLM V1 decode step on 2x Quadro RTX 6000 (TP2, NVLink), Qwen3.8-27B-class hybrid model (8 full-attention layers with head_dim 256, 24 Q / 4 KV heads; 24 GDN linear-attention layers) ... batch 4-8, ctx 512-2048, CUDA graphs on" on "TU102 / sm_75 (Turing) ... 535 GB/s DRAM ceiling, CUDA 13.3"; the ~4.3 ms residual is "STRUCTURE (split-softmax workspace round-trip to DRAM, a second combine launch, step serialization), not bandwidth"; "attention's KV traffic is only ~0.12 ms at the DRAM wall"; "Sensitivity floor learned empirically: only multi-millisecond per-step deltas move end-to-end rows." Sibling record gdn-step-coupling.json (2026-09-14) banks the #step-profile gap ledger and the #surgeries line "graph-structure fixes" — this item is the fork/join half of that surgery set.
lacuna.current_status: Read 2026-09-15. Fork/join inside one CUDA graph is a first-class, documented, arch-independent mechanism. Capture-side: work may fork across multiple streams during cudaStreamBeginCapture, but every branch must join before capture ends (NVIDIA DL CUDA Graph docs, 'Stream Fork-Join Model'); cross-stream cudaEventRecord/cudaStreamWaitEvent calls during capture become graph edges (PyTorch issue #114320 documents the captured-event semantics; Juelich CUDA-graphs course material demonstrates the fork pattern). Replay-side: the captured streams do not exist at replay — topology alone orders execution (NVIDIA forum thread 293965), so a replay into one stream still runs captured branches concurrently. Overhead numbers are small and dated: without graphs each launch costs ~5-10 us CPU-side; graphs reduce this to one host submission per replay, with straight-line graphs launching in constant time (NVIDIA blog 'Constant Time Launch for Straight-Line CUDA Graphs', CUDA 12.0-era, 2023); device-side per-node cost remains ~1 us class (Hazy Research measured graphs cutting GPU-side launch ~2.1 -> ~1.3 us, 2025-05-27; practitioner counterexamples: StackOverflow 78648536 reports a dependency-heavy captured graph SLOWER than the equivalent event/stream loop; HN thread 44112409 complains of ~us-class replay node costs) — so event/fork nodes cost microseconds per replay, irrelevant at a 24.3 ms step. Tooling state: raw CUDA supports all of it on CUDA 13.3 / sm_75; PyTorch's high-level torch.cuda.graph captures on ONE side stream and multi-stream capture is not supported by torch.compile (open feature request #170241); manual multi-stream capture under torch.cuda.graph is possible with strict fork/join discipline (side.wait_stream(current) entering, current.wait_stream(side) exiting — NVIDIA 'CUDA Graph Best Practice for PyTorch' quick checklist and 'Capture Failures' docs) but interacts badly with the caching allocator: record_stream during capture leaks memory (pytorch#155398), and graph private pools pin capture-time addresses (RFC #51075). vLLM V1 state: piecewise CUDA graphs (PR #20059; design doc page dated 2026-06-23) default to FULL_AND_PIECEWISE — a FULL graph for uniform decode (this host's batch 4-8 decode case) and pieces between splitting_ops with attention outside pieces for other shapes; capture and replay are single-stream, and the doc nowhere mentions multi-stream concurrency — nothing in vLLM V1 exploits intra-graph parallelism for a TP dense step. The engine's only intra-step concurrency is Dual Batch Overlap (DBO, --enable-dbo; design doc v0.12.0; vLLM blog 2025-12-17: DeepSeek Wide-EP at 2.2k tok/s/H200; v0.18.0 notes DBO now works with all models): split the batch 2+2 at the model runner, two worker threads, overlap one micro-batch's attention/communication with the other's compute — built and measured for communication-hiding at EP scale, not for dense small-batch TP2 (arXiv 2605.21603 evaluates DBO on DeepSeek-V2-Lite across two GPUs with expert parallelism).
lacuna.applicability: Transfers fully at the mechanism level: fork/join capture, event edges, and event nodes are pure scheduling with zero architecture dependency — they work identically on sm_75/CUDA 13.3, unlike every other acceleration lever in this frame. Concretely available on this host: (a) the uniform-decode step already replays as one FULL graph on one stream, so branch concurrency must be authored INTO the capture (raw CUDA or the NVIDIA best-practice side-stream pattern under torch.cuda.graph — the torch.compile automatic route does not exist, #170241); (b) the natural branch is DBO-style batch 4-8 -> two micro-batches, so micro-batch A's latency-bound attention kernels (KV traffic ~0.12 ms, latency-not-bandwidth-bound) run concurrently with micro-batch B's weight-streaming Marlin GEMMs, and symmetrically for the 24 GDN layers; (c) a second, cheaper branch: the walk kernel's splits are internally parallel — no graph needed there — but TP2 allreduce latency can hide under subsequent compute via a forked NCCL branch if the step profile shows exposed allreduce gaps. What does NOT transfer: DBO's published wins (they are allreduce/all-to-all hiding on NVSwitch/EP fabrics — a TP2 NVLink pair's per-layer allreduce is tiny, and the GEMM lane is already pinned at the 535 GB/s wall, so there is little idle resource for a second micro-batch's GEMMs to use); torch.compile multi-stream capture; any expectation of launch-overhead savings (graphs already on — fork/join adds ~1 us-class node costs). The candid framing: vLLM V1's single-stream serial replay does leave overlap on the table by design, but on THIS workload the concurrently-runnable work is small — the priority question is whether the #step-profile ledger shows multi-ms of serially-idle SM time (e.g. GDN kernels with idle SMs waiting on the 2-CTA-law attention phases) that a fork/join could fill [uncertain].

design.mechanism: Authoring, raw-CUDA route (recommended for the owned kernels): capture the whole decode step per batch size with cudaStreamBeginCapture(mode=thread_local) on the capture stream; fork a branch with cudaEventRecord(fork_ev, cap); cudaStreamWaitEvent(branch, fork_ev); launch branch work on the side stream; join with cudaEventRecord(join_ev, branch) + cudaStreamWaitEvent(cap, join_ev) before the sampler; instantiate and replay exactly as today. Branch content, in order of expected value: (1) DBO-shaped 2+2 micro-batch split — micro-batch A's attention walk/combine (the owned pair) on the branch while micro-batch B's Marlin GEMMs stream on the main stream, swapped each layer; requires per-micro-batch static input/output buffers allocated from the graph's private pool and a scheduler that assigns requests to micro-batches stably across steps (replay expects identical topology). (2) Allreduce-under-compute fork for TP2 if #step-profile shows exposed NCCL gaps. PyTorch route (engine-level DBO experiments): inside torch.cuda.graph, side_stream.wait_stream(current) -> with torch.cuda.stream(side): branch ops -> current.wait_stream(side); never call record_stream during capture (#155398 leak); use capture_error_mode='thread_local' or 'relaxed' (the default 'global' mode forbids unrelated-stream work during capture). Event/fork nodes add ~1 us each per replay — use freely; the budget is 24.3 ms.
design.failure_modes: (1) Replay safety is structural: any kernel that reaches the GPU outside the captured topology at replay time races the graph — every branch op must be INSIDE the capture, and inputs must live at capture-time addresses (static buffers; the piecewise-bug class vLLM fixed repeatedly, e.g. commit 73b3569a 'cudagraph expecting inputs at capture-time addresses'). (2) Capture legality: forgetting the join, or an un-synced side stream, fails capture (NVIDIA 'Capture Failures': stream management is the most common capture failure); fork/join must be strictly nested. (3) Allocator: cross-stream tensors during capture leak via record_stream (#155398) and private pools pin addresses (#51075) — pre-allocate all branch buffers before capture. (4) Occupancy coupling: co-scheduling attention (which lives under the 2-resident-CTA law) with Marlin CTAs on the same SMs lets GEMM CTAs evict/starve attention CTAs and stall its pipeline — the falsified 'KV pipelining NEGATIVE' result rhymes: concurrency added around the hot path measured negative once here already; the branch must be chosen so the two halves want DIFFERENT resources (latency-bound attention vs streaming GEMM), not the same ones. (5) Bandwidth: at the 535 GB/s wall a concurrent branch steals bytes from weight streaming; the overlap win is bounded by the smaller branch's non-bandwidth time (~0.12 ms attention KV traffic + kernel latency) — sub-ms unless GDN phases are large and idle [uncertain]. (6) Numerics: no math change within a micro-batch, but the 2+2 split changes TP allreduce grouping order -> tiny logit drift; if batch-invariance is asserted anywhere (cf. FlashInfer issue #2107 requesting batch-invariant decode), the split must be excluded from those paths.
design.effort_estimate: Gate-1 cull ~10 min: read the #step-profile ledger for (a) total SM-idle time inside the step and (b) whether GDN/attention phases leave resource headroom while Marlin streams — if idle time is sub-ms, cull without writing code. If it survives: raw-CUDA two-stream capture of the owned walk/combine pair as a branch probe, kernel-lane 1-2 days; full DBO-shaped engine restructure (scheduler micro-batching + static buffers + capture plumbing), engine-lane 3-5 days.
design.priority_signal: Against, on the published record: every measured fork/join-in-decode win (DBO, Wide-EP) is communication-hiding on fabrics this host does not have; the step's critical path is ~9 GiB/rank of Marlin weight streaming already pressing the 535 GB/s wall, and the independently-runnable work (attention KV ~0.12 ms) sits two orders of magnitude below the multi-ms sensitivity floor; the falsified levers (KV pipelining NEGATIVE, bandwidth levers) both warn that adding concurrency to this step has already lost once in-engine. For, conditionally: the frame names 'step serialization' as part of the 4.3 ms residual and fork/join is the ONLY mechanism in this research set that attacks serialization without kernel rewrites, it is fully arch-independent (no sm_90 excuse), and event-node costs (~1 us) are noise at 24.3 ms; if the #step-profile ledger shows the 24 GDN layers' kernels leaving SMs idle against Marlin's streaming phases, a 2+2 micro-batch fork could reclaim multi-ms in one graph-authoring change. Decision rule: no ledger evidence of multi-ms concurrent-runnable idle, no build.
